changes.summary: A page that breaks now returns a real error page — it says the fumble is on our end and gives you a button to try again, instead of the same “Page Not Found” card a mistyped URL gets.
Owner Activity is now site analytics: league traffic, per-owner engagement, page reach and app installs — and no transaction leaderboard.
Owner Activity is now site analytics: league traffic, per-owner engagement, page reach and app installs — and no transaction leaderboard.
Front Office now opens straight into your League Planner — extensions, free agent needs, cap metrics and draft assets — with every contract and trade tool one click away in the sidebar.
changes.headline: Front Office is now your League Planner's home
changes.lede: One page for the whole offseason: extensions, free agent needs, this year's cap picture and next year's draft assets, switchable to any team in the league — with contracts, trades and every salary tool a click away.
changes.imageAlt: TheLeague's Front Office page showing the team switcher, Extensions and Veteran Extension Candidates cards, and the Front Office Tools sidebar

changes.summary: Front Office now opens straight into your Keeper Planner — drag players above the line to keep them — with Rosters, Trade Builder and the Keeper Report Card a click away.
changes.headline: Front Office is now your Keeper Planner's home
changes.lede: Drag your 7 keepers above the line and everyone else gets cut when you finalize — right on the page Front Office now opens to, with Rosters, Trade Builder and the Keeper Report Card one click away.
changes.imageAlt: The AFL's Front Office page showing the Keeper Planner's above-the-line keeper slots and the below-the-line cut list, with the Front Office Tools sidebar

changes.summary: Signed-out visits are counted now — Owner Activity shows how much of the traffic comes from people who never sign in, and which public pages they read.
Players on injured reserve no longer count against your active roster when you add a free agent — the form now shows how many active spots you actually have.
The game line on Set Lineup now leads with the network's logo at text size and closes on a bigger opponent helmet — the channel was reading as the headline.
Live Scoring showed no fantasy matchups during the Wednesday opener — the board now loads its scores directly and keeps polling on any game night.
Owner Activity no longer slides sideways on a phone — the Last Seen table scrolls on its own now, instead of dragging the page with it.
Team logos on Owner Activity are no longer circle-cropped — every club's mark shows in full, corners and all.
League dates now follow the official NFL schedule — 2026 opened on a Wednesday, so Roger no longer announces the season a day late, and deadlines and playoff weeks track the real calendar.
The AFL calendar had Regular Season Ends on Dec 31 — two weeks after the playoffs start. It now reads Dec 17, when Week 14 closes and the bracket opens.
Schefter can no longer pair a team with a player it doesn't roster — trade-rumor posts now check ownership against the rosters before naming anyone.
Schefter runs at most one trade story a day now, across every lane — and the invented trade-speculation pieces drop to one a week.
Schefter's trade-speculation posts now open the Trade Builder with the named team loaded, instead of linking back to the post you just read.
Live Scoring's matchup view now runs edge-to-edge on a phone — tighter header, roomier player rows, and one more starter on screen without scrolling.
Free Agents on mobile: the waiver status is now a small badge you tap for details, so the page gets to the player list without a wide banner running off-screen.
Free Agents' toolbar on mobile now fits into two tidy rows instead of three, with Watch List grouped by the view toggles and My Rank by the action buttons.
New Schedule page: your own season week by week with scores and next opponent, plus the whole league's grid.
The homepage hero is game day again — Schefter's weekly recap and previews no longer take it over as breaking news, so that slot is back to real trades and auction wins.
Schedule now prints the final score in every grid cell, and a season picker reaches back through every season on record — so old scores are two clicks away.
My Schedule on Schedule now wears your club’s colours and crest instead of the league’s — the league grid keeps the league look.
On Sunday Ticket, the league and country pickers are now one line each that you swipe left and right, instead of five rows of chips above the board.
New Live Broadcast: a second-screen TV board watching every league you’re in — scores, a full-screen reveal when your player scores, a lower-third when your opponent’s does.
The Live Broadcast board has a Full screen button for TVs with no keyboard, four games at full size with the rest on one compact row, and three quiet controls instead of a chip per league.
Fixed a crash that blanked the next page with a red error box when you left Set Lineup for your Roster or any other page.
Fixed a mix-up for owners in both leagues: switching leagues from Set Lineup or Players could leave the league you just left still driving the page.
Fixed live scores on the Live Broadcast board resetting to 0.0 and creeping back up: one league's feed blinking no longer wipes that league's numbers off the screen.
Fixed projected scores on the Live Broadcast board reading exactly the same as the live score, which pinned every win-probability bar to 100%.
The Live Broadcast board now shows each team's own "to play" count on its row, and one matchup clock that counts down the football you have left instead of the last game to kick off.
Team names on the Live Broadcast board no longer truncate beside empty space — the name and its "to play" count take the row's spare width, and the numerals stay flush right.
The Tuesday recap hero now opens the week that just finished — that week's scoreboard, every matchup with final scores — and it names the week that was actually played.
Division standings now badge all four playoff teams in each conference — the AL was showing one wild card instead of two, and seeding both leagues off one shared ladder.
Schefter no longer hands out season honors mid-season — Top of the Standings, Scoring Champ and Cellar Dweller now wait until the season is actually over.
Schefter's columns now know which league they're covering — AFL articles were being written by a reporter told he worked for a 16-team league called TheLeague.
Signing in now returns you to the page you were headed for instead of the homepage — from any link, any button, or a session that expired mid-action.
A commissioner-only page now tells you it's commissioner-only, instead of silently bouncing you to the homepage with no explanation.
Schefter no longer re-posts a once-a-season column after it ages out of the feed — the 2026 schedule release went to the group chat a second time mid-season.
Schefter scans, the rumor mill and Roger lineup reminders are running again after a CI install failure silenced them from Sep 11–15.
Owner Activity was dropping visits from some browsers, so owners who use the site read as never visiting. Those visits count now.
The Auction view on Free Agents now leaves the page when the offseason auction closes and returns on its own when the next one opens.
Player names on the Front Office planner open the full player card now, and a ⋮ menu on each row manages your own players or adds a free agent to your watch list.
The AFL's Front Office planner now carries Roster at a glance plus NFL and College Stacks — your age curve, and which of your players share a team.
The AFL Front Office page no longer slides sideways on a phone — a long player name now truncates inside its card instead of pushing the whole page over.
Free Agents was showing last season's snap counts — GP, Snaps and Snap% now track the season being played, and each column is stamped with the year it reports.
Free Agents now shows GP, Snaps and Snap% for every player, so you can see who is actually on the field before you claim them.
The AFL Front Office planner now fits two keeper cards per row instead of three, so player names read in full — and its filter bar stacks when the panel is narrow.
Offseason War Room now opens with League Planner and Rosters — the cap, contract and salary tools live inside the planner rather than in their own menu section.
The planner at the top of Offseason War Room is now called Front Office everywhere — menu, footer and search all point at the same page.
Your Throwback Week era now sits on Preferences, right under your clock — same cards, same instant save, one page for all your settings.
Free Agents swaps the empty "Last Yr" column for total points — the current season once it kicks off, last season before that — and it finally counts free agents.
Projected Free Agents was reporting double points — a doubleheader week counted every performance twice. The totals are now the real ones.
The AFL footer now links Front Office under My Team — it was reachable from the menu only.
AFL rosters now carry a Total column — season points to date — and Avg is a real per-game average instead of last week’s score.
The Coach tab on Roster & Salary Cap has a new Total column — season points to date, sortable, beside the per-game Avg.
In dark mode the Coach tab’s Avg, weekly-score and opponent labels were near-black on the dark table. All three now use colors that invert with the theme.
